**Summary of extracted program graphs:**

The specification was the README for the Current Finance (Pebble Protocol) Sui Move lending contest. I read the README plus 8 key source files to extract 10 functional units:

| ID | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| SG-001 | `enter_market` | Obligation creation — validates version, emode, circuit breaker, creates shared Obligation + ObligationOwnerCap |
| SG-002 | `deposit` | Collateral deposit — mints ctokens via exchange rate, updates liquidity mining rewards |
| SG-003 | `borrow` | Asset borrow — accrues interest, validates emode membership, enforces health factor and min_borrow_amount |
| SG-004 | `withdraw_as_coin` | Collateral withdrawal — burns ctokens, checks health factor post-withdrawal |
| SG-005 | `repay` | Debt repayment — accrues interest first, handles partial/full repay with overpayment refund |
| SG-006 | `liquidate` | Normal liquidation — soft liquidation bounded by close_factor, seizes ctokens, splits protocol fee |
| SG-007 | `flash_loan_lifecycle` | Flash loan borrow+repay — hot potato pattern enforces same-PTB repayment, fees tied to emode |
| SG-008 | `accrue_interest` | Reserve interest accrual — simple interest model, monotonic borrow index, idempotent per-block |
| SG-009 | `obligation_deposit_ctoken` | Obligation ctoken state — mutual exclusion of collateral/debt per asset type |
| SG-010 | `liquidate_adl` | ADL liquidation — separate permission, two modes (debt ADL vs collateral ADL) for bad debt scenarios |

Key invariants captured across all graphs:
- Circuit breaker halts all user-facing operations when triggered
- A single CoinType cannot be both collateral and debt in the same obligation (enforced even under flash loan reentrancy per the contest spec)
- Users cannot switch emode once obligations are created
- Only assets from the obligation's emode group can be borrowed
- Borrow index is monotonically non-decreasing
- Flash loan amount strictly less than cash (reserves can be borrowed)
- Soft liquidation: repay capped so risk level returns to exactly 1.0
